question: All people have their rights, but it is better for all of us that different sorts of people should keep to their own kind.
essay:
I disagree with the idea that people should “keep to their own kind.” While everyone has the right to live freely and pursue happiness, dividing people into separate groups by race, culture, religion, or background does not make society better. In fact, it usually leads to misunderstanding, fear, and unfair treatment.

Human beings are not improved by isolation. When different sorts of people live, work, and learn together, they share ideas and develop respect for one another. Diversity helps communities become stronger because people can learn from different experiences and perspectives. A society that welcomes difference is usually more creative, more tolerant, and more just.

The claim that people should stay among their own kind also ignores the fact that such divisions are often based on prejudice rather than truth. It suggests that people are naturally incompatible, when in reality most conflict comes from lack of understanding. If people separate themselves, those misunderstandings grow worse. If they come together, they have a better chance of building trust.

Of course, every person has the right to choose their own friends, culture, and way of life. But that does not mean groups should be kept apart. Rights should protect freedom, not enforce division. The better path for all of us is not separation, but respect and cooperation across differences.

In short, people are not made safer or happier by staying apart. A fair society depends on inclusion, not isolation.
label: Strongly disagree
